sentences.text: Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 9307 of 2022 Applicant :- Surendra Kumar Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar Singh,Abhishek Kumar Mishra,Chandrakesh Mishra,
Ji Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ajay Kumar Srivastava Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court on 22.03.2021.

3. Submission of the counsel for the applicant is that even as per the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C, prima facie, no offence can be said to be made out under Section 376 A-B I.P.C. read with Section 5/6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter referred to as, 'POCSO Act').

entities.text: Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He argues that at the worst even if for the sake of argument the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. is treated to be correct the offence could come within the category of Section 7/8 of POCSO Act and cannot be termed as an aggravated sexual assault as defined under Section 3, 4 & 5 of the POCSO Act.

He further argues that after rejection of the first bail application, only five witnesses out of 12 have been examined so far.

entities.text: Surendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He draws attention of the Court to the statement of the doctor, who was examined as P.W.5, which is prima facie not corroborating the F.I.R. version, however, from the facts that emerge that the applicant is in custody since 06.12.2020 and almost three years has passed and there is no likelihood that the trial be concluded in near future.
4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the fact that the mandate of Section 35 (2) of POCSO Act has also been violated in the present case, which is evident as only five prosecution witnesses out of 12 have been examined so far and on a very consideration of statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the medical report and the fact that the applicant has already undergone in incarceration for three years, the applicant has no criminal history and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Surendra Kumar be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No. 432 of 2020, under Section 376 A-B I.P.C. read with Section 5/6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act,
Police Station Gajraula, District Pilibhit subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 17.8.2023 Mustaqeem.
